title: SSE abrupt-close causing concatenated JSON events and event-id reuse for hosted API
creator: Maya Chen
description: Multiple customers reported production failures when using the Hosted API streaming endpoint: client-side parsers receive concatenated JSON objects (two events joined with no newline/sep) and the server occasionally reuses event IDs for different logical events after an abrupt connection close. This causes downstream parsers and dedup layers to either reject the stream or produce corrupted partial outputs. The incidents started after the 2.4.0 kernel changes to the output buffer flush path and increased under high-concurrency bursts.
observed_behavior: When a TCP/SSE connection is closed mid-chunk (network blip or proxy teardown), the server flush path sometimes emits the incomplete tail of the pending buffer directly appended to the next session's outgoing buffer. Clients see merged JSON objects like '{"type":"token"} {"type":"token"}' or a reuse of an event-id header leading to dedup miscounts. Some customers see their parsers throw JSON parse errors; others treat as partial tokens and never recover, resulting in failed requests and elevated error rates.
expected_behavior: On abrupt closes, the server should flush only complete SSE event frames, fence any incomplete fragments, and never reuse event-ids or memory regions across connections. Clients must receive cleanly delimited events or explicit end-of-stream markers so they can recover or retry safely.
reproduction_steps: Run a small load generator against hosted-stream endpoint with concurrent clients (50+) and enable induced TCP resets via iptables to simulate mid-chunk close.
Capture raw bytes on the wire with tcpdump for sessions that experienced resets.
Replay captured stream into a local client that uses a strict SSE/JSON event parser and observe parse failures and concatenated messages.
Run the above with runtime-2.3.9 (baseline) and runtime-2.4.0+ to confirm regression in flush behavior.
root_cause_summary: A combination of an aggressive zero-copy flush path and a shared output buffer pool introduced a race: when a connection aborted during an in-flight flush, the buffer's tail pointer was not fenced before returning the buffer to the pool. A subsequent write could reuse the same buffer slice and append without inserting the required SSE delimiter or allocating a fresh event-id. The change in 2.4.0 that bypasses a copy for small chunks widened the race window.
proposed_fix: Introduce per-connection fencing: mark buffers as 'in-flight' until the drain confirmation from the socket layer is observed or a timeout expires.
Ensure atomic write of SSE delimiters and event-id headers; always copy incomplete fragment tails into a per-connection hold buffer before returning the shared buffer to pool.
Add an invariant check in debug builds that validates buffer ownership and a replay/poison value when reusing buffers to catch regressions early.
Patch includes a small perf regression mitigation: only allocate hold buffer on detected fragmentation paths; common fast-path remains zero-copy when no mid-flush aborts occur.
rollout_plan: Create feature branch with fixes and unit + integration tests (runtime-2.4.2-hotfix).
Deploy to internal canary region (staging-hosted) with 5% traffic and enhanced telemetry for buffer reuse and invalid SSE frames.
If no degradation in latency or throughput and no invalid frames seen for 48h, promote to 25% then 100% over 6 hours.
Coordinate with ops to enable immediate rollback if error rate increases or CPU/latency degrade >10%.
Notify top impacted customers about a maintenance window and remediation timeline.
test_plan: Unit tests covering buffer fence logic and explicit copy-on-abort paths.
Integration test that injects synthetic TCP resets and validates no concatenated events are emitted.
Load test at customer-like QPS to measure latency and CPU delta vs baseline; assert <5% throughput regression.
Synthetic customer reproduction harness that validates client parsers receive well-formed events for 10k sequential connections with randomized aborts.
monitoring_and_metrics: New metric: sse.invalid_frame_count (count of stream frames that failed SSE/JSON parse at the gateway).
New metric: buffer.reuse_poison_hits (debug-only boolean counter to detect buffer reuse after return).
Alert: alert if sse.invalid_frame_count > 10 in 5m for hosted region or if client parse error rate increases by >200% from baseline.
Dashboard: per-region breakdown, customer top-n by error volume, correlation with tcp reset/syn-rst rates.
updates: 2026-03-10: Triage — customer escalation from three customers (retail search, chat widgets, internal eval) reporting parse errors under bursts. Assigned to Liam. P0 declared.
2026-03-11: Reproduced locally with iptables resets; captured concatenated JSON objects in tcpdump; preliminary heap dump shows buffer slices shared across connections.
2026-03-12: Narrowed regression to zero-copy flush change in commit a7b9d2 (runtime-2.4.0); wrote failing unit that reproduces ownership race.
2026-03-13: Implemented fence + copy-on-abort prototype; integration tests pass; perf microbench shows ~2% p95 latency increase in worst-case but no throughput regression.
2026-03-14: Opened draft PR #2146 for review; preparing staging canary. Notified affected customers with ETA for patch deployment.
